derivation: apparently from G4219 (πότε) and the base of G4226 (ποῦ);
def: interrogatively, whatever, i.e. of what possible sort

occurrences.text: But the men marvelled, saying, What manner of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him!
And as he went out of the temple, one of his disciples saith unto him, Master, see what manner of stones and what buildings are here!
And when she saw him, she was troubled at his saying, and cast in her mind what manner of salutation this should be.

Now when the Pharisee which had bidden him saw it, he spake within himself, saying, This man, if he were a prophet, would have known who and what manner of woman this is that toucheth him: for she is a sinner.
Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness,
Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
